gloss: to complain; to grumble; to gripe

definitions.gloss: to complain; to grumble; to gripe
definitions.explanation: To express dissatisfaction or complaints, especially about things one cannot change, often to someone who will listen sympathetically.

examples.japanese: {愚痴|ぐち}を{言|い}っても{仕方|しかた}がない。
{彼|かれ}はいつも{仕事|しごと}の{愚痴|ぐち}を{言|い}う。
{友達|ともだち}に{愚痴|ぐち}を{言|い}って{少|すこ}し{気|き}が{楽|らく}になった。
examples.english: I felt a little better after venting to a friend.

examples.japanese: {愚痴|ぐち}ばかり{言|い}っていないで、{自分|じぶん}から{行動|こうどう}を{起|お}こしなさい。
examples.english: Stop just complaining and take action yourself.

notes:
{愚痴|ぐち} originally comes from Buddhist terminology meaning spiritual ignorance or foolish attachment. In modern usage, it refers to complaints or grumbling, particularly about things that cannot be easily changed. Saying {愚痴|ぐち}を{言|い}う implies a certain futility — the speaker knows complaining won't solve the problem but does it anyway.

The verb can also be {愚痴|ぐち}る (a casual verb form meaning "to gripe"), which is common in informal speech.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {愚痴|ぐち}を{言|い}う: to complain
- {愚痴|ぐち}をこぼす: to let complaints slip out
- {愚痴|ぐち}を{聞|き}く: to listen to someone's complaints
- {愚痴|ぐち}ばかり{言|い}う: to do nothing but complain
- {愚痴|ぐち}っぽい: prone to complaining

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {文句|もんく}を{言|い}う: to complain; to object — more confrontational, directed at a specific target
- {不平|ふへい}を{言|い}う: to express dissatisfaction — more formal
- {愚痴|ぐち}る: to gripe — casual verb form of the same concept
